title: Error about freed objects captured by lambda is confusing (and may be better as a warning)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e]

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.3.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M2 - Apple M2 (8 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

If a lambda is created that captures a variable, and then the object stored by that variable is freed, then when the lambda is called an error will be given to the user, like this:
```
E 0:00:01:295   scene.gd:11 @ _ready(): Lambda capture at index 1 was freed. Passed "null" instead.
  <C++ Source>  modules/gdscript/gdscript_lambda_callable.cpp:110 @ call()
  <Stack Trace> scene.gd:11 @ _ready()
```
The error takes a bit of work to parse out, and I think could benefit from better wording as a result. At the very least, replacing the index of the capture with the symbol name would make it clearer to the programmer what is going on.

Alternatively, this behavior may be better as some kind of warning, rather than an error. There are cases where the programmer may want to run code at a later time, which checks if a captured variable has been freed, and runs some code if not. Currently, even if the programmer implements their checks inside the lambda, the error will still be generated because it is captured at all in the lambda.

### Steps to reproduce

The below GDScript produces a runtime error:
```gdscript
extends Node2D

func _ready() -> void:
	var node_a = Node2D.new()
	var node_b = Node2D.new()
	node_b.queue_free()
	
	var lambda = func(): print(node_a, node_b)
	await get_tree().create_timer(1.0).timeout
	lambda.call() # Lambda capture at index 1 was freed. Passed "null" instead.
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp-lambda-capture-error_2026-03-25_13-25-36.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26253966/mrp-lambda-capture-error_2026-03-25_13-25-36.zip)
